Primary Question: Is this extracted article technically usable and trustworthy enough to enter the annotation pipeline?
What Must Be Built: Automated rule engine for title/body/date/canonical/source/provenance/GCS checks; extraction-quality scoring; exception queue; parser-version linkage
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Fully automated first pass using deterministic validation and anomaly rules across 100% of records
Human Review: Small human audit sample plus review of flagged anomalies/failures; humans validate the automation, not label every record
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations or extraction_quality_reviews linked to article_versions; auto_status, auto_reasons, rule_version, confidence, validation_status
Reviewer UI: /review/l0 focused on sampled audit and exceptions rather than routine manual labeling
Quality / Evaluation: Automated pass/review/fail rates by source; sampled human validation accuracy; parser-defect rate; false-pass/false-fail rate
Entry Criterion: Collected article version exists with provenance
Exit Criterion: Automated L0 decision stored for 100% of records; validation sample shows acceptable performance; unresolved hard failures excluded
Downstream Use: Automated corpus-quality gate before all semantic layers
Proposal / Research Link: Preprocessing, provenance verification and data-quality control

Primary Question: Is the article substantively about a Kenyan event or issue within the study population?
What Must Be Built: Gazetteer/NER evidence engine plus geographic relevance classifier; confidence thresholds; uncertainty queue
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automated across 100% using Kenyan place/institution/demonym evidence, foreign-location evidence, NER and a classifier/score; publisher identity alone must not decide
Human Review: Small stratified validation sample across sources/languages/confidence bands; ambiguous/low-confidence cases prioritized for human review
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations (task_type=kenya_relevance) + human_validation; preserve suggested_label, confidence, evidence, model/rule version
Reviewer UI: /review/l1 for sample validation and uncertainty review, showing article, detected evidence and automated label
Quality / Evaluation: Accuracy/F1 against human validation sample; ambiguity rate; confidence calibration; subgroup error rate by source/language
Exit Criterion: Automated Kenya-relevance label exists for all eligible records and validation performance is acceptable
Proposal / Research Link: Target population = eligible articles reporting/discussing Kenyan events/issues

Primary Question: Does the eligible Kenyan article report or substantively discuss GBV under the approved study definition?
What Must Be Built: Versioned weak-supervision bootstrap + reviewed/mixed-label dataset export + AfroXLMR binary classifier; configurable thresholds; uncertainty sampling; reproducible model artifacts and lineage. The reviewed/mixed exporter and real trained model are the immediate missing pieces.
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Weak supervision covers all 324 L1-Kenya versions with original labels 7/15/302. Current Human Review overlays those outputs to 10 gbv / 312 not_gbv / 2 borderline. For training, latest resolved human labels must take precedence; unreviewed machine binary labels may be used only under an explicit mixed-effective policy with provenance. Human borderline/unresolved records remain excluded from binary training.
Human Review: All 302 originally borderline weak results now have a recorded review, producing 3 reviewed gbv, 297 reviewed not_gbv and 2 reviewed borderline. This review coverage is operational evidence, not an independent final reference set. Future sampling must preserve a held-out human subset for final evaluation and may prioritize uncertainty/disagreement/rare groups.
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations + human_validations now; reviewed/mixed development manifests and future frozen reference/adjudication datasets; preserve machine annotation ID, latest human-validation ID, label source, guideline version and exact L1 prerequisite
Reviewer UI: /annotations/l2 and /annotations/review/<annotation_id> already support effective-vs-machine views and protected confirm/correct workflow; future work adds explicit dataset export/sampling/adjudication support
Quality / Evaluation: Initial model: training diagnostics and bounded inference only if class support is too small for a defensible validation split. Final evaluation: independent human-reference precision/recall/F1, macro-F1/AUC where supported, calibration, false-positive/negative analysis, subgroup metrics and learning curves.
Exit Criterion: Primary L2 predictions available for the eligible corpus with documented provenance, validated thresholds and independent reference-set performance
When to Build: Reviewed/mixed export now; first AfroXLMR development model next; iterative retraining while scaling toward ≥5,000
Downstream Use: Binary target used for downstream L3/L4 candidate selection and active-learning prioritization
Proposal / Research Link: Objective 1; human-supervised via explicit review provenance, sampled validation and later held-out evaluation

Primary Question: For GBV-positive articles, what form(s) of GBV are reported?
Label Structure: Multi-label probabilities + thresholded labels for approved GBV taxonomy
What Must Be Built: Automated multi-label classifier using AfroXLMR/XLM-R; taxonomy-specific output head; per-label thresholds; versioned predictions
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automated across 100% of L2-positive records. Initial weak/rule labels can bootstrap training; final annotation is produced by the multi-label model
Human Review: Small stratified validation sample including rare classes, multi-label cases and low-confidence predictions; humans correct sampled outputs
Suggested Database Objects: model_predictions/automated_annotations with per-label probabilities, threshold version, model_version; human_validation and final_reference_labels separate
Reviewer UI: /review/l3 for validating sampled multi-label outputs, low-confidence cases and rare categories
Quality / Evaluation: Per-label precision/recall/F1, macro/micro-F1, label-support/imbalance analysis, calibration and human override rate
Entry Criterion: L2 automated GBV-positive or borderline record
Exit Criterion: Multi-label predictions stored for all included records with acceptable validation metrics and documented thresholds
When to Build: After L2 classifier baseline is available
Downstream Use: Automated GBV-type analytics and training/evaluation target
Proposal / Research Link: Proposal requires one or more applicable GBV-type categories

Primary Question: Where did the reported event occur, and which place mentions are event locations rather than contextual locations?
Label Structure: Detected spans + location role + normalized place/admin unit + confidence
What Must Be Built: Gazetteer/rule baseline + contextual NER + event-location role classifier + Kenyan gazetteer/disambiguation + geocoding
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Baseline can begin on an initial usable L2-positive candidate pool. Final automated processing targets L2-positive records after the L2 classifier is validated; NER extracts toponyms, event-role logic identifies incident locations, geocoder resolves admin units.
Human Review: Sample human validation, oversampling ambiguous/multi-location/low-confidence cases; validate spans, event-vs-context role and normalized/geocoded admin units.
Suggested Database Objects: location_predictions / extracted_locations / geocoded_locations + human_validation; preserve span offsets, role, normalized name, confidence and model/geocoder versions
Reviewer UI: /review/l4 planned; reuse the current review principles with detected spans and map/admin candidates
Quality / Evaluation: Entity precision/recall/F1, exact-span match, event-role accuracy and admin-unit geocoding accuracy against human reference spans
Entry Criterion: Initial usable L2-positive pool for baseline; validated L2 positives for final evaluation
Exit Criterion: Automated location outputs produced with acceptable validation metrics and documented error boundaries
When to Build: Start baseline after initial L2 model output; can proceed in parallel with L3 and corpus scaling
Downstream Use: Location model evaluation and privacy-safe map aggregation
Proposal / Research Link: Objective 2: separates place extraction, event-location interpretation and geocoding

Primary Question: Does the article or derived output contain information that should be hidden, generalized or withheld?
Label Structure: Multi-label privacy-risk flags + automated action + confidence
What Must Be Built: Automated PII/risk detection using NER + regex/rules + location-precision checks; suppression/generalization policy
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automated across 100% before downstream display/API. Use high-recall PII detection and rule-based output actions
Human Review: Small high-risk audit sample plus mandatory review of low-confidence/conflicting cases where policy requires it
Suggested Database Objects: privacy_risk_predictions / safety_flags + human_validation; action, reason, confidence, policy_version, model_version
Reviewer UI: /review/l5 for sampled high-risk validation and policy exceptions
Quality / Evaluation: Recall on known sensitive patterns, false-negative audit, override rate, audit completeness, zero unnecessary PII in public outputs
Exit Criterion: Automated safety decision attached to every displayable record; validation confirms acceptable protection
When to Build: Design alongside L2-L4; enforce before dashboard
Proposal / Research Link: Proposal requires data minimisation, privacy protection, aggregated geography and human oversight

Primary Question: How well do automated annotations match human judgement, and where does automation fail?
Label Structure: confirmed/corrected/unresolved decision + human label + error type + adjudicated/frozen reference label where available
What Must Be Built: Current protected review workspace plus explicit reviewed/mixed export, future stratified/uncertainty sampler, reviewer assignment, adjudication and calibration reports
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automation selects/organizes random-stratified, uncertainty-focused and disagreement-focused samples; the full corpus remains primarily machine annotated. Current L2 review covers every originally borderline weak record but is not by itself an independent evaluation sample.
Human Review: For L2, 302 originally borderline records now have saved reviews: 3 current reviewed gbv, 297 reviewed not_gbv and 2 reviewed borderline. Future review should add representative confidently classified positives/negatives and preserve a separate held-out human reference subset; full-corpus human correction is not required.
Suggested Database Objects: human_validations now; reviewed/mixed dataset manifests next; future validation_samples, annotation_adjudications, reviewer metadata and frozen reference-label membership
Reviewer UI: Current /annotations/review/<annotation_id> supports L0/L1/L2 confirm/correct, effective-vs-machine views and history; dedicated sampling/adjudication/reference-freeze workflow remains future work
Quality / Evaluation: Human-human agreement on double-coded subset where available; automated-vs-human accuracy/F1 on independent samples; correction/override rate; calibration; error categories and source/language subgroup metrics
Exit Criterion: Validation statistics and known error boundaries documented; final held-out reference subset frozen and isolated before thesis evaluation
Downstream Use: Provides evidence that automated annotation is credible and human-supervised without manually labelling the full corpus
Proposal / Research Link: HITL through review/correction, active learning, calibration and independent held-out evaluation

Primary Question: Can every automated label, human validation and model result be traced to its source and version?
What Must Be Built: Dataset manifest; annotation export/version; duplicate groups; deterministic split; held-out test isolation; prediction lineage
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automate manifests, hashes, prediction lineage, duplicate grouping and split generation
Human Review: Researcher approves version freeze; human-reviewed reference sample and held-out test remain isolated from later tuning
Suggested Database Objects: dataset_versions, corpus_membership, split_assignment, duplicate_group_id, model_version, annotation_version, guideline_version
Reviewer UI: Admin/report page showing corpus/prediction versions, counts and split status
Quality / Evaluation: No duplicate leakage; complete provenance; reproducible labels; isolated held-out reference set
Entry Criterion: Automated annotation + validation performance acceptable and corpus large enough
Exit Criterion: Immutable/versioned development data and isolated evaluation/reference sets exist
When to Build: Before final model comparison and thesis evaluation
Downstream Use: Reproducible experiments, error analysis and final evaluation
Proposal / Research Link: Supports corpus versioning, auditability and held-out evaluation
